title: Maya-S v1.1.41 with --parallel 2: 14h real agent traffic + controlled smoke

hardware.pcie: engine-measured link 28.8 GB/s per card (x8 gen1 on this board)

soak.traffic: real agent sessions routed via a local gateway; two long-context sessions overlapped for most of the window
soak.decode_band_under50_note: gen<50 band shows 120.5 solo vs 31.0 concurrent; short generations are dominated by draft-window and step-interleave effects, recorded but not quoted as a rate

smoke_controlled.cold_vs_warm_note: first fresh 42K reads right after boot measured 1,336-2,106 tok/s vs the warm soak median 3,538 at the same size; 1.1.41 #612 improves first-read vs 1.1.40, but we did not A/B the versions

official_comparison.claim: v1.1.36/1.1.37 release notes: DSpark draft batching under --parallel, ~1.1x aggregate on two lanes (3x V100); per-lane cost around 78% in the community-reported shape
official_comparison.ours_controlled_probe: 93-99% per lane (identical tiny prompts, both lanes idle otherwise)
official_comparison.ours_real_traffic: 66% per lane (median, generation >=200 tokens, prefill-interleaved agent traffic)
official_comparison.reading: both sit within the official order of magnitude; the real-traffic figure is the one to copy into planning

limitations: L1 soak is observational real traffic, not a scheduled benchmark: solo/concurrent split comes from the engine's own 'conversations running' field; concurrent-lane requests skew toward the two heavy long-context sessions.
L2 all rates are engine-log counters (prompt N = reused + read in X ms; generated in Y ms). API wall-clock differs up to ~30% and is never mixed in.
L3 512K window only (max observed 478,303 tokens = 91.2%); no 1M test, no --parallel 4.
L4 two-lane aggregate capacity is inferred as ~1.3x a single lane from the measured per-lane medians; we did not run a fixed-workload throughput benchmark.
L5 PCIe link on this board runs at 28.8 GB/s (x8 gen1); CPU-lane traffic is heavier than a full-width link, which mainly costs prefill depth.
L6 engine was stopped at 09:59 for a GPU handoff, so the soak end is an operational stop, not a timeout.
